setting: A fictional client meeting about changing the scope and timing of a project.

presentation.situation: You manage {{project}}. {{a}}, the client director, wants it {{earlier}} earlier with no extra budget. {{b}} is the client's technical lead. You could {{options}}. Find out why, offer a fair trade, and confirm what is agreed.
presentation.opening: We need {{project}} {{earlier}} earlier, and we cannot increase the budget.

brief.you_are: You are the project manager, and you can agree changes to scope and timing.
brief.situation: You manage {{project}}. {{a}}, the client director, wants it {{earlier}} earlier with no extra budget. {{b}} is the client's technical lead. You could {{options}}. Find out why, offer a fair trade, and confirm what is agreed.
brief.task: Find out what really matters to the client, offer a fair trade-off rather than simply saying yes, and confirm the agreement.
brief.done_looks_like: You know their real priority, you agreed a trade, and you have confirmed exactly what changes.

participants.name: You
participants.relationship: You are the project manager, and you can agree changes to scope and timing.
goals: Find out what really matters to the client, offer a fair trade-off rather than simply saying yes, and confirm the agreement.

card.want: To hit the date, without paying more.
card.attitude: Firm and commercially minded, and reasonable when given a real trade.
card.speech: Fluent, natural professional English. Direct, and free of corporate slogans.
tactics: State the demand firmly at first
Accept a trade only if the key priority is protected

pressure.gentle: Patient. Gives the other person time.
pressure.balanced: Pushes back once on anything vague.
pressure.challenging: Keeps pressing for specifics, fairly and without insults.

card.want: A delivery that actually works, even if some features come later.
card.attitude: Pragmatic, and more flexible on scope than the director.
card.speech: Fluent, natural professional English. Direct, and free of corporate slogans.
tactics: Say which features could wait, if asked

pressure.gentle: Patient. Gives the other person time.
pressure.balanced: Pushes back once on anything vague.
pressure.challenging: Keeps pressing for specifics, fairly and without insults.

ledger.text: The client wants it {{earlier}} earlier, and will not increase the budget.

objectives.evidence: The learner asks a question that uncovers the underlying priority.
alternatives: What matters most about that date?

objectives.evidence: The learner offers a conditional trade-off.
alternatives: If we move some features to a second phase, we could hit that date.

objectives.evidence: The learner confirms the agreement explicitly.
alternatives: To confirm: we launch the core by the new date, and the rest comes after.

signals: \b(?:what matters most|which is more important|your priority|why is)\b
opportunity: Are you going to ask why we need it earlier?
Why do you think the date matters?
beats.orient: I've made a demand. Before you answer, find out why. Ask what matters most about the date.
fallback: Why do you think the date matters?
Are you going to ask why we need it earlier?

beats.goal: Hear a trade rather than a concession.
opportunity: So can you do it or not?
beats.orient: Now offer me a trade. Start with: If we. You could change scope or timing, as in your brief.
fallback: So can you do it or not?
beats.second_line: Some of the features could wait, if that gets us a working launch.

opportunity: So what exactly have we agreed?
Can you put that in one sentence?
beats.orient: Now confirm exactly what we agreed. Start with: To confirm.
fallback: Can you put that in one sentence?
So what exactly have we agreed?

closing_line: Good. That works for us. Please send that in writing.

o1.good: Asking why, before you say yes or no.
common_mistakes: Saying yes or no straight away
o1.micro_lesson: Ask: What matters most about that date?
o1.model: What matters most about that date? What happens if we miss it?
o1.smaller_step: Say: Why does the date matter?

o2.good: Linking what you give to what you get.
common_mistakes: Agreeing to everything, or refusing everything
o2.micro_lesson: Say: If we, then we could.
o2.model: If we move two features to a second phase, we could hit that date.

o3.good: Saying the agreement aloud, so that it can't be misunderstood.
common_mistakes: Ending on: That should be fine
o3.micro_lesson: Say what changes, and who does what.
o3.model: To confirm: we launch the core on the new date, and the rest follows a month later.

variants.options: move features to a second phase, or reduce testing scope with the client's agreement
variants.need: A trade show on the new date is where the system will be shown to customers.

variants.options: launch to one department first, or postpone the mobile version
variants.need: A new group of staff starts on the new date, and they need the portal for their first day.
